description:
A wallet's WalletConnect session is scoped to one chain (for example Ethereum mainnet, chain 1), but signing requests that name a different chain are still shown to the user and signed instead of being rejected.

Step 1. A dApp opens a WalletConnect session scoped to chain 1 (Ethereum mainnet).
Step 2. The same dApp sends a signing request (personal_sign / eth_signTransaction) that names chain 137 (Polygon).
Step 3. The wallet displays the request and, when the user approves, signs it. It does not reject the out-of-scope chain, and it silently switches the network context for the request.

Impact: a user who believes they are signing on mainnet can be tricked into signing on another chain where the same address holds funds or where a malicious contract is waiting. The wallet is the last line of defence for chain scope, and it does not enforce it. Reproduced 19 out of 19 attempts in a local test harness against the session handler.

expected.note: Anonymised from a real filed report (WalletConnect chain-scope, Low / CWE-284). The mock stub should return valid/low; live SERV may refine severity.

title: WalletConnect session processes signing requests on chains outside the session scope
